item.title: About
item.description: I spent 25 years keeping mission-critical systems alive — carrier-grade wireless networks, signaling infrastructure, prepaid databases running on Solaris and HP-UX, across telecom deployments in six countries. The discipline that comes from that world — SLA management, ITIL, eTOM, the assumption that failure is not hypothetical — is the foundation everything else here is built on. I’m now retooling deliberately into cloud-native and modern software engineering. That means: 42 São Paulo — an intensive, project-based systems programming curriculum: C, algorithms, memory management, Unix/Linux internals, peer-reviewed code with no lectures and no shortcuts.
